title: Future Group targets scale in latest super fund integration
full_text:
Future Group has continued its consolidation strategy, announcing the Guild Retirement Fund will transfer into the Smart Future Trust from 12 September as it seeks to leverage greater scale across its superannuation business.
The successor fund transfer (SFT) will see the GuildSuper and Child Care Super brands remain in place, preserving their focus on the pharmacy and early learning sectors while moving members onto a shared operating platform.
Future Group said the change is designed to deliver operational efficiencies without disrupting the member experience.
The transaction is the latest step in Future Group’s strategy to streamline its operations with the group now supporting more than 400,000 members and manages around $14 billion in superannuation assets across five brands.
Chief executive Simon Sheikh said increasing scale enabled the group to invest more in members while lowering duplication across the business.
“As we grow, we can use that scale to reduce duplication, increase our negotiating power with service providers and continue investing in services and investment capabilities for members.
“This latest transfer builds on the successful SFT of the Future Super Fund into the Smart Future Trust last year. It is another important step towards a simpler and more scalable structure across Future Group.
“GuildSuper and Child Care Super will retain the brands, member relationships and industry focus that make them distinctive, while benefiting from the scale and operating capabilities of a larger structure behind the scenes.”
The transfer follows the migration of the Future Super Fund, which underpins the Future Super and Verve Super brands, into the Smart Future Trust in May 2025.
Members will also see changes to the funds’ fee structure from 12 September. The annual dollar-based administration fee will fall from $72.80 to $67.60, while the 0.02 per cent administration cost currently paid from fund reserves will be removed.
At the same time, the percentage-based administration fee deducted from member accounts will increase from 0.15 per cent to 0.16 per cent a year.
The administration fee cap will increase from $800 to $1,000 a year and will apply only to the percentage-based fee. Future Group said the overall impact for members would vary depending on their account balance and investment option.
As part of the transition, GuildSuper and Child Care Super members will also gain access to a revised MySuper LifeStage investment approach with four age-based options, alongside an updated Choice investment menu.
